finding.claim: Missing await on async authorize() in DELETE /reports/:id. The 403 rejection is never awaited, so the delete runs regardless of grants. Any authenticated user can delete any report. The rejected promise is also unhandled, which can crash the process on newer Node versions.
finding.source: Authenticated low-privilege user sends DELETE /reports/:id with any report id (req.params.id)

trace.note: report loaded by attacker-supplied id, no ownership scoping
authorize() called without await; its returned promise is discarded, so the thrown 403 does not stop the handler
sibling PUT handler awaits authorize, which shows the intended control

finding.guards_checked: authorize() throws on missing grant (server.js:11-14), but the call at line 20 is not awaited or error-checked, so it is not enforced. The sibling PUT handler awaits it correctly. There is no other middleware-level authorization.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 throws 403 on a missing grant, but the call at line 20 is not awaited, so the throw becomes an unhandled rejection and the handler continues. The only other middleware (server.js:4-7) sets req.user and does no authorization.
verdict.reason: server.js:20 calls async authorize() without await, so its 403 throw (server.js:14) never stops server.js:21 db.reports.remove, and any authenticated user can delete any report, unlike the awaited call at server.js:27.

finding.claim: Authentication is never enforced. The middleware copies req.session.user into req.user without checking it exists, and no session middleware is installed. An unauthenticated request leaves req.session undefined, so the middleware throws and returns a 500. If a session is present but has no user, req.user is undefined and authorize() throws a TypeError on user.id. This is a fail-closed crash for PUT and an unhandled rejection for DELETE. For DELETE, authorize is not awaited, so an unauthenticated or anonymous session can still delete reports (see F1). This is mostly an aggravating factor for F1 rather than a separate exploit.
finding.source: Unauthenticated request with a session that has no user

trace.note: req.user = req.session.user with no presence check
user.id dereferenced inside authorize; TypeError becomes a rejected promise that DELETE ignores

finding.guards_checked: There is no login-required middleware, and no session middleware appears in the file. Only PUT fails closed, because it awaits authorize.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 throws on a missing user (TypeError at :10) or a missing grant (403 at :14). The DELETE handler calls it at :20 without await, so the rejection is discarded. PUT awaits it at :27 and so fails closed. There is no login-required middleware and no session middleware in the file.
verdict.reason: server.js:5 copies req.session.user without a presence check, and server.js:20 calls authorize without await, so a missing user or missing grant never stops db.reports.remove at :21. This only applies when a session object exists, which the file never installs (without one, :5 throws and every request gets a 500), and the real harm is the missing await already tracked as F1.
